attempts.entry_title: Hippocampal and prefrontal maps across a novel and a familiar W-maze (Tang, Shin and Jadhav 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Tang, Shin and Jadhav (2023) on dandiset 000447, which holds CA1 and prefrontal units, position and trial tables of five rats running a W-maze alternation task in a novel, a familiar and again the novel room. It compares spatial maps across environments, Bayesian decoding with novel-room templates, selectivity and path equivalence of single cells, UMAP manifolds of the pooled populations, and cross-condition generalization. The de novo learning sessions and the second group of rats behind Figure 1 are not in the dandiset.

findings.statement: The units table's `electrodes` column holds tetrode numbers, not row indices of the electrodes table as the NWB format requires, its values run up to 64 in ZT2, whose table has 128 rows (two per tetrode), and up to 30 to 32 in the others. Read as row indices, up to 32 units per animal are put in the wrong region; read as tetrode numbers, the counts match the paper's (98 CA1 and 171 PFC cells against 99 and 171 here).

Units carry no cell number within a tetrode, no waveform and no putative-interneuron label, so the paper's interneuron exclusion (spike width and rate in the Methods, per-animal (tetrode, cell) lists in its code) cannot be applied. Units clustered only in later epochs are appended to the table with no spike in N (1 to 19 per animal), without a note.

In every file `acquisition/ElectricalSeries` is a byte-identical second copy of the 1.5 kHz LFP in `processing/ecephys/LFP`, stored at a different offset; there is no 30 kHz spike-band recording, and the copy roughly doubles the file sizes.

The position's reference frame is given as "center well", but positions are camera coordinates in which the center well lies at different places in each epoch (for example AM2 (32, 52) cm in N and (73, 86) cm in F). The five files' session start times fall within 16 minutes on 2023-03-14, two days before the first published version, which is the time of conversion, not of recording.

The files hold no linearized positions, idealized track paths or trajectory labels per position sample, no sharp-wave ripple or theta times, and the epochs carry no names (N, F and N' are known only from the dandiset description's order). The paper's rate maps, decoding and manifolds use all of these; here linear positions had to be rebuilt from the 2D positions and ripple times could not be excluded.

In AM2 the electrode groups Tetrode26 to Tetrode31 carry the labels tetrode27 to tetrode32, so group names and labels disagree; electrode descriptions are placeholders ("my description", "no description").

The de novo learning sessions of the five rats and the behaviour of the three F-N-F'-N' rats (Figures 1B, 1C, S1B, S1C) are not in the dandiset; four claims are blocked and one is tested on the N-F-N' day only.

decoding_position_novelfamiliar_trial_batch.m (Figure 2F) takes the last ten trials of the pre-switch epoch only `if ep == 1`, but runs on epochs 2 and 4, so it always takes the first ten N trials, against its own comment ("last 10 trials") and the legend's switch from N to F. With the last N trials CA1 error rises at the switch (Dunn p = 0.0021); with the first ten it does not (p = 1).

Question for the authors. What is the width of the 1D Gaussian that smooths the linearized rate maps? The text reads "s = σ cm". Results were run at 8, 4 and 2 cm; figs4d, figs5e, fig3d and fig3e change outcome with the width and are blocked for it.

Question for the authors. How were the idealized paths for linearization defined, and are the linearized positions available? They are not in the dandiset; here W-shaped paths were built from the well and run positions.

Question for the authors. In Figure 2F, are trials -10 to -1 the last ten N trials (as the legend and the code's comment suggest) or the first ten (as the code runs)? CA1 error rises at the switch with the last ten (p = 0.0021) but not with the first ten (p = 1).

Question for the authors. In Figure S3D, which novel trials are shown (N, N' or both), how are trials numbered across animals with different numbers of passes, and which is the last trial? CA1 similarity falls over trials of N or of N' alone but not over N then N'.

Question for the authors. Does Figure S5F use the signed or the absolute selectivity index? Path equivalence is uncorrelated with the signed SI but negatively correlated with its absolute value in PFC (p < 0.0001).

Question for the authors. For the ramping cells of Figure S4, which positions enter the regression and which cell samples form the denominator (495 and 636)? The rule as written gives 3 to 8% of cell samples here, against 16.4 and 18.1%.

Question for the authors. For the geometric random model of Figure S7, in which space are the axes permuted (the 3 UMAP coordinates or the neurons), and what happens to the cluster centres (the legend says rotation-translation)? Its code is not in the repository.

Question for the authors. How were the single-trial rate maps behind the UMAP manifolds smoothed, and were 1-cm bins that hold no position sample within a pass filled or left empty? The Methods say only that bins with spikes from fewer than 5 neurons were discarded. The PFC CCGP of Figure 4D fails clearly with 8-cm smoothing (9 of 16 decoders) and comes within one decoder of passing, or passes, with 2-cm smoothing (15 or 16 of 16, depending on the embedding), and without filling the PFC parts of Figure 3H and 3J fail at 2 cm.

entries.title: Hippocampal and prefrontal maps across a novel and a familiar W-maze (Tang, Shin and Jadhav 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Tang, Shin and Jadhav (2023) on dandiset 000447, which holds CA1 and prefrontal units, position and trial tables of five rats running a W-maze alternation task in a novel, a familiar and again the novel room. It compares spatial maps across environments, Bayesian decoding with novel-room templates, selectivity and path equivalence of single cells, UMAP manifolds of the pooled populations, and cross-condition generalization. The de novo learning sessions and the second group of rats behind Figure 1 are not in the dandiset.
